name: Religious communism
summary: Religious communism holds that common ownership of goods is commanded or modelled by religion, most often by the Jerusalem church of Acts, whose members shared everything and gave to each as he had need. Its adherents live or seek to live in voluntary communities of goods, work the land together and reject buying, selling and hired labour as a betrayal of faith. Within this family, the Hutterites and Winstanley's Diggers renounce force, while Müntzer's peasant movement took up arms.
scope: The mainstream Christian strand: the Jerusalem church of Acts, the Hutterite colonies, and Winstanley's Diggers, with Müntzer, the Taborites and Oneida noted as variants. Islamic, Buddhist and Taiping cases, and Marxist-religious blends, are excluded. Because these groups wrote little on modern policy, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Care for the sick is a communal duty in the shared-goods ethic, but the sources never discuss state health systems; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Winstanley rejected hired labour altogether, so a higher wage floor is beside the point; sources are silent on wage law.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Winstanley condemned buying and selling of land and Christian communists cite love of money as the root of evil, so market allocation is rejected on principle.

public-ownership.rationale: Goods are held in common, but by the community or congregation rather than the state, so state-owned industry fits only loosely.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Acts has the rich sell and give to those in need, implying redistribution from wealth, but taxation by a state is not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Religious communists were rarely concerned with trade unions; communal work replaces the wage relation unions bargain over.

property-fundamental.rationale: Acts 4:32 says no one claimed any possession as their own, directly denying private property as a fundamental right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations are not addressed; the movements aimed at abolishing commerce for profit rather than regulating it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Sharing so that none lacks need is the core ethic of the early church, so cutting aid for fear of dependency is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Working the land together and holding the product in common resembles collective ownership by those who labour, though the unit is the community.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Communal groups seek separation from state intrusion, though Hutterite colonies themselves police conduct closely; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Hutterite and similar communities impose strict moral rules, while Diggers said nothing; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear strand position.

strong-leader.rationale: Winstanley held that no person should rule over another, and Hutterite colonies elect and can remove their leaders.

state-harmful.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites distrust rulers and worldly separation, but few strands call for abolishing all government; they run their own disciplined communities.

limit-guns.rationale: Nonresistance is a tenet for Hutterites, but gun law is not addressed; Hutterite farms commonly hunt and keep rifles.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nonresistance bars Hutterites from military roles and Winstanley abhorred force, so more military and police power is disfavoured.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Communal religious groups hold strict sexual morality; inferred from Hutterite discipline.

decide-locally.rationale: Decision-making sits in the colony or congregation, with its own council and vote, favouring small local self-rule.

rehabilitation.rationale: Forgiveness and mercy in the Christian base suggest reform over punishment, though Acts 5 shows severe judgement.

traditional-family.rationale: Hutterites keep patriarchal family units, but Taborites, Oneida and Diggers varied; strands are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditional communal churches such as Hutterites reject it; inferred, with modern Christian communists dissenting.

abortion-legal.rationale: Conservative communal churches oppose abortion; inferred, as sources do not address it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is the source and centre of the movement, and communities organise life around scripture, though they seek separation from the state.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equality of all people under God supports redress, but sources do not discuss racial history.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Communal churches ground roles in scripture; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Loyalty is to the religious community, not the nation; Hutterites preserve their own language and customs instead.

gradual-change.rationale: Movements aimed at an immediate reorganisation of life on communal lines rather than slow reform of existing institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Worldly separation implies little trust in worldly institutions; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Buying and selling for gain is condemned by Winstanley and by Christian communists citing 1 Timothy 6:10.

nation-first.rationale: Universal brotherhood under one God cuts against national self-interest, though nationalism is not discussed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nonresistance and rejection of force make military intervention difficult to endorse even for rights.

open-borders.rationale: Universal equality favours it in principle, but communities guard membership; sources do not address borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; frugal communal life fits, but no stated position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Hutterites adopt technology selectively and put faith above progress; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites renounce armed force, though Müntzer in the Peasants' War is a violent counter-example, so the mainstream is against.

experts-over-public.rationale: Winstanley held that each person has the same inner reason as any ruler, against deference to elites.

central-planning.rationale: Communities coordinate production inside the colony by consent, not by a state plan; a central state plan is not their model.

socialized-markets.rationale: Winstanley rejects markets altogether, while Hutterite colonies trade with outsiders; split.

land-value-tax.rationale: Winstanley wanted land common, not taxed; the tax is not discussed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Sharing of goods in the church implies no hoarding for heirs; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution by need exists in the church but through community, not state payments; not addressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy between states is outside what Acts, the Diggers or Hutterites wrote about; neutral.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Colonies direct their own investment and keep apart from the state; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They favour common ownership, not many small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Winstanley rejected giving or taking hire, and Hutterites work without paychecks, though money is still used for outside trade.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Money systems are not discussed by the sources beyond the condemnation of usury; no position either way.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class bodies are foreign to voluntary religious communities; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Communities are governed by their congregation and elected ministers under scripture, not a party; Winstanley rejected rule of one over another.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Taborites rejected their king and Winstanley denied any right of one to rule another.

democracy-best.rationale: Hutterite colonies vote internally but not on liberal terms; adherents place divine law above majorities.

direct-votes.rationale: Colonies decide major matters by membership vote, but the sources do not extend this to national lawmaking.

workers-councils.rationale: Colony councils exist, but they are religious not workers' councils; not addressed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Communities sought separation from the world; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Winstanley stated all are equals in creation and none was ordained to rule another.

political-violence-never.rationale: Winstanley abhorred arms and Hutterites hold nonresistance, though Müntzer's strand was violent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of force reject war as ennobling.

separate-church-state.rationale: Hutterites and Anabaptist-descended groups hold worldly separation and keep the state out of the church, though they want exemptions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hutterite Ordnungen and scripture-based rules govern life in colonies; they seek a society ordered by scripture, not state law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hutterites avoided secular courts, yet no stand on private provision of defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: One humankind under one God contradicts ethnic nationhood; not discussed directly.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, and class conflict is not its explanatory frame; Engels read Müntzer that way instead.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution according to need and equals in creation imply approximate material equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: None of the sources discuss indigenous peoples' land claims, so the strand has no stated view.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources never address colonial debts; the strand's sharing ethic is not applied to them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Fellowship is of believers within a community; not political union of nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement rests on renouncing private gain, with the love of money condemned as evil.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Members owe the community obedience under the Ordnungen and share goods as a duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Winstanley saw earth as a common treasury given for all, valued by use; not clearly addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; Hutterites farm with modern equipment, Diggers pre-date it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Selective adoption is the Hutterite practice; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Conservative religious groups wary of transformation of the body; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by inner reason and consent of community, not machines; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A modern technology question that these communities never took up; no inferable position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Many strands look back to the Jerusalem church or Eden as a model, yet others aimed at a new order; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Scripture rather than results guides adherents; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Diggers occupied commons and began working the land themselves rather than petitioning Parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: Winstanley said community would be built by working together, without force.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Diggers and Hutterites are agrarian, not foragers.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Colonies assign roles by gender and office, and not abolish them.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Acts 2:45 and 4:35 say distribution was made to each as he had need, the founding text of the strand.

production-for-use.rationale: Common treasury and working together for all to eat describes production for use not profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Winstanley treated hired labour as upholding the curse and profit from trade as unrighteous.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, and its voluntary and religious strands do not seek class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Diggers worked land together and Hutterite colonies farm collectively as the main economic form.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a doctrine of the strand; Marxist claims are not its own.

taxation-theft.rationale: Hutterites refuse to pay taxes for war but accept ordinary taxes; not a principle.

harm-principle.rationale: Colony rules regulate whole lives and conduct beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Community takes priority and rights lie in the congregation; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Nonresistance bars Hutterites from military service and led them to emigrate from Russia over conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Members may leave but are shunned; voice is limited; mixed.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts the rejection of buying and selling for gain.

positive-liberty.rationale: Meeting need so that none lacks is the ethic, but freedom language is not used.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source says anything about media or universities as centres of power; neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equality under God contradicts racial hierarchy; not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Colonies are governed by councils and elected bosses, but this isn't family-and-trade-body representation.

total-state.rationale: Communities seek separation from the state and refuse state control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; nation is not the unit.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority is not by oaths to lords, and Winstanley rejects lording.

bound-labor.rationale: Winstanley denied any person's right to labour owed to another, calling for equals.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources treat knowledge as grounded in scripture or inner anointing, not in power, so no clear answer on this claim.

universal-morality.rationale: God's commandments are treated as binding on all humankind; inferred from scripture-based grounding.

single-common-good.rationale: One heart and soul and a common treasury aim at one common good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora and return rights are not a topic in any of the sources; neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hutterites maintain German as a church language, but national revival is not addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Colonies hold member votes and elect their managers, who can be removed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Hutterites run own colony schools, but vouchers are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy of states is outside the movement's concern, which is community life; neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Freedom of the market is rejected; liberty is found in community of goods.

rule-by-example.rationale: Early church and colonies rely on exemplary conduct and discipline rather than state law; Winstanley used inner reason.

national-self-determination.rationale: The community of believers, not the nation, is the unit of self-rule, so the sources give no answer on national states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious communism springs from principles native to religion; Winstanley grounded his case in inner anointing.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Need is met regardless of origin in the ethic of equals; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Those who work share together, and the Hutterite community expects labour from members, but need is met for all; split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class conflict is not its frame; but wage employment is rejected.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural institutions and their trade-off with other goals are never discussed; neutral.

dominated-front.rationale: Alliances of states against Western powers are outside the sources; neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Believers are one humankind; neither national nor class lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hutterite colonies are patriarchal while Taborites and Winstanley's equality point the other way; split.

ban-interest.rationale: The biblical condemnation of usury is cited by Christian communists as a basis against interest.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist doctrine rather than a religious communist one; but Winstanley saw rulers as oppressors.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not addressed by these historical or agrarian movements; neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Hutterites resist assimilation of themselves; not addressed for others.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims are not part of the strand.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems of national legislatures are not addressed; colonies vote internally, which is a different matter.

national-mission.rationale: Worldly separation and nonresistance counter mission by state.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Winstanley supports equality while Hutterites are patriarchal; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Winstanley and the Diggers saw rulers and landlords as oppressors of the poor.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Equal moral worth of all persons.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources do not discuss legal accountability of governments for past abuses; neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mutual care for need is a duty, not left to a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Winstanley called all equals in creation and Christian communism stresses one humankind.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate not relevant to the strand.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a category is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Communities seek their own law and exemptions, but no stance on civil code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Anabaptist-descended groups stress voluntary membership and religious liberty for themselves.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Hutterites farm livestock for food; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hutterites run their own religious teaching and separate from the state; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a socialist state in the Soviet sense, and rejection of state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Colony leaders are elected and removable by member vote; Winstanley rejected rule imposed by one on another.

trade-surplus.rationale: Commerce for gain is not an aim.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorring arms mean initiating force is wrong, though property rights are not the reason.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fellowship and sharing replace struggle for gain.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Communities seek exemptions from the state, so empowering it to ban parties is not favoured.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Winstanley said none should lord over another, matching non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design of state powers is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party is Marxist-Leninist, whereas religious communism acts by congregation and conscience.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distribution to need so that none lacks, with the poor central in the early church.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Sharing in common is preferred over individual home ownership; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and picketing belong to wage labour, which the strand rejects rather than regulates; no position.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Winstanley blamed buying and selling and landlords for want, not numbers.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; Hutterite ministers are chosen by lot in some branches but this was not confirmed in sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; Hutterites sought exemptions from state power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price setting is not discussed; the strand abolishes selling rather than fixing prices, so neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party control is alien to the strand and the Hutterites want to keep outside control from their lives.

party-commands-army.rationale: The strand rejects armies and party rule.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: State citizenship rules are not a concern of the sources; neutral.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Winstanley's equality implies rulers do not stand above others; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Church discipline binds members but parties are not the model.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions of states are not addressed in the sources; neutral.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hutterites are led by elected ministers and a bishop council, but congregational strands differ; split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hutterite colonies are led by elected ministers but are not clerical rule over the state; split.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan, not part of the strand; nonresistance but no stated stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Hutterite colonies ban television and limit internet for morals but would not turn to state censorship; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents are not in the sources; neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Hutterite ministers and bosses are elected and can be removed by vote.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nonresistance and separation from worldly powers.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Diggers and Hutterites chose agrarian communal life as the model.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National division and reunification is not discussed; neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hutterites limit schooling at around age 15, yet no stated stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources do not take up ranking of cultures; neutral, though Christian universalism cuts both ways.

death-penalty.rationale: Nonresistance and mercy; though Acts 5 shows divine death, state execution is not backed; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Scripture-based communal groups would favour it; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Strict moral discipline in colonies; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

minority-language-support.rationale: Hutterites maintain their German church language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Hutterites repeatedly sought exemptions on photo ID and military service.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conformity is enforced through Ordnungen and shunning.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Biblical debt relief and jubilee ethos; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting national constitutions is not a topic in the sources; neutral.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sharing with those in need is the ethic of the movement.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms make a national nuclear arsenal incompatible with the Hutterite and Digger stance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How a head of state is chosen is not discussed; neutral, since the strand rejects rulers more broadly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank governance is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nonresistance favours peace over territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In Acts property is sold and brought to the community so that none lacks.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The strand sets itself against Marxism but the sources say nothing on how to classify the Soviet Union; neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances conflict with nonresistance, so an attack on one ally being an attack on all is rejected.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International law on annexation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hutterites resist state control and secular courts, with the state curbing church property disfavoured.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The figure of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nonresistance means military force cannot be used to hold a region, whatever the political merits.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special arrangements for regions within a state are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Winstanley held no one is to lord over another.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wealth is to be shared; a flat tax favours the rich; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources attribute change to conversion and shared life rather than giving a theory of character; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule by one over others rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a communal religious goal; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed by the sources; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a human ruler runs against equality and God as sole authority.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not in the sources and Hutterite family roles are patriarchal; neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist topic not at issue.

land-redistribution.rationale: Winstanley wanted land held in common and taken from those who monopolise it, though by peaceful occupation.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Universal brotherhood in Christian communism opposes claiming land for ethnic kin, an inference as no source discusses it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hutterites shun those who leave but stress voluntary membership; the state punishing is not backed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Hutterite women wear head coverings by custom, not law; split.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed by the sources; neutral.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Colonies seek their own culture and institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy of this kind is not addressed; neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Contrasted with Marxist materialism; they hold religious principles drive change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Monopoly policy within markets is not discussed; the strand rejects markets as such, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not addressed by the sources; neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Taborite equality of the sexes and Hutterite male-only voting point opposite ways, so no common answer.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Colonies are largely self-sufficient farms; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements are not discussed; neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work is done from fellowship and love rather than pay, as in colonies where members receive only allowances.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Taborites rejected feudal lords and Winstanley rejected one lording over another.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hutterite schooling teaches scripture and basics, with no stated stance on national history teaching; neutral.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Winstanley's equality of all and the universal brotherhood in Christian communism rule out tutelage, inferred as no source takes it up.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty to community and God over nation; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preference policy is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed beyond the condemnation of usury; neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism is condemned as based on love of money, but the sources do not discuss its adaptation.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not found in the sources on religious communism; neutral.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights entrenchment is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era borders are not discussed; neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Colony leaders are elected, and rulers by inheritance are not favoured.

minority-veto.rationale: Hutterite decisions by vote of members, but unanimity is not required; split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Taborites and Müntzer resisted, whereas Winstanley and Hutterites renounce force.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Winstanley's equality placed no one above, and Hutterites put scripture over legislation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in the sources, and colonies farm livestock; neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty of the rich to give is stated, but the paternalist hierarchy is rejected by equals; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hutterites hold worldly separation and avoid political involvement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Hutterites ban television for moral reasons, but not framed this way.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is Marxist and absent from the sources on religious communism; neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is not part of the strand and the sources do not discuss it; neutral.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for state office is not addressed; neutral.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns Marxist parties' national paths, which is not the strand's concern; neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms mean territory cannot be taken back by force; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political leadership by pre-colonial peoples is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional founding values of states are not addressed; neutral.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources contrast religious communism with Marxism but say nothing about comparing totalitarian regimes; neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender disadvantage debates are not in the sources; neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cultural fit of political institutions is not addressed; neutral.

paid-care-work.rationale: Colonies treat care work as communal service without pay; split.

filial-duty.rationale: Strong family duty in colony life; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service selection is not addressed; Hutterite officers are elected, which is not an exam system; neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of firms is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Colony officers can be removed by vote of the members.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Sharing in common provides for the old, not individual savings.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget powers are not addressed; neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy of states is not addressed, and Hutterites keep German for worship; neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is held in common in the strand, but foreign ownership is not addressed; neutral.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law doctrine is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Giving up possessions and the love of money condemned.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms rule out funding armed groups abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nonresistance and abhorrence of arms rule out troops entering allied countries without consent.

corporate-influence.rationale: Rich and merchants are criticised; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Regulation of foreign funding of NGOs is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Large families valued but state incentives not discussed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed, though colonies limit membership.

job-guarantee.rationale: All work together and none lacks; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Theories of international relations are not addressed by the sources; neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Hutterite colonies teach obedience under the Ordnungen, though they refuse state demands that violate conscience.

non-intervention.rationale: Separation from the world and nonresistance.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation is not discussed in the sources because the strand rejects hired labour; neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Winstanley and Christian universalism offer no basis for conspiracy accusations against a minority; inferred from equal worth.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Church marriage is central to colony life.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Government transparency law is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

local-production.rationale: Colonies produce for themselves from local land.

informal-organisation.rationale: Diggers formed small voluntary groups working land together.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Relation of national and international law is not addressed; neutral.

religious-nation.rationale: They separate the believing community from the nation.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Oneida members kept few personal items and Hutterites have personal allowances, though all else is common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Adherents are communists in their own sense, and see religion as the source.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Needs are met by the community, not market mix; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religious communism is contrasted with Marxism, which called for eliminating religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Capitalism is condemned as founded on love of money.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Winstanley and Taborites emphasise equality yet the strand rarely links it to economics; split.

socialized-care.rationale: Hutterite colonies share communal meals and care; strands differ.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed, and Hutterites use German and English freely; neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state are not addressed; neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing communal settlements are the central form: Jerusalem church, Diggers, Hutterite colonies.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They call themselves communists, though not in the Marxist sense.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Religious ties to land as political claims are not addressed in the sources on religious communism; neutral.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Conservative strands would disapprove, but state punishment is rejected by others; split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Church discipline exists but state enforcement is contrary to separation; split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Equal standing of all in creation and rejection of lording rule out governing territories for another's profit; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Nonresistance; the Islamic strand differs, but the mainstream is Christian.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Colonies decide by member votes; Winstanley's equals.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not in the sources; neutral.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The sources do not frame their politics by left and right; neutral.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx compared work in common to a remedy, and the strand condemns hired labour.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Winstanley and Hutterites ground authority in God, not human rulers.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Hutterites seek religious exemptions and practices.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment law on nondisclosure is not addressed in the sources, and the strand rejects employment; neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nonresistance means members take no part in military activity, which fits abolishing armies though states are not told what to do.

dynastic-succession.rationale: No ruling of one over another.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Usury condemned and common aid favoured.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from priority to the poor.

property-franchise.rationale: Winstanley's insistence that all are equals in creation excludes limiting the vote to owners, and the strand rejects private property in land.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are not in the sources; neutral.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept of commodity relations that the sources do not use, though the strand opposes buying and selling; neutral.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Rich wealth over poor criticised; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The rule of published laws is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equality of all in creation (Winstanley) and one humankind rules out a racial franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Digital deliberation is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

open-government-data.rationale: Open government data is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hutterites discourage outmarriage by community rules, but law is not their tool; split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Equality of all in creation rules out boycotts targeting a group, inferred as no source discusses it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deliberative assemblies of chosen citizens are not discussed; neutral.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Hutterites hold to old rules; modern Christian communists differ.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Winstanley said land kept in the hands of a few is theft.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is central to the strand, opposed to Marxist elimination.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Winstanley and nonresistance reject force, but no sources on abolishing police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational government is not discussed by the sources; neutral.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Winstanley made the earth a common treasury and Hutterite colonies own land as a body, so individuals hold it only as members.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial independence is not addressed by the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Acts and the Hutterite colonies meet need through voluntary sharing inside the believing community, with no state role.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed; the strand mostly rejects rulers, and Hutterite ministers serve by community choice, so no stance is inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Hutterite colonies decide by direct member votes, so handing one's vote to another is inferred to be foreign to them.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; its providential view of history and its focus on community life give no clear lean.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The living Hutterite case reserves ministry to men, though Diggers and some other strands varied; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Hutterite family roles are patriarchal, and the other strands wrote little against it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; the Hutterites keep apart from worldly politics and the sources are silent on local voting.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: Winstanley refused to take or give hire and rejected buying and selling land.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from Acts 4:32, where no one claimed anything as his own.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the Hutterites practise nonresistance and Winstanley's movement renounced force.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the nonresistance of the Hutterites and Diggers, though Muntzer took up arms.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the nonresistance of the Hutterites and Diggers.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: a faith of justice and brotherhood would affirm recognition of such wrongs.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Winstanley and the Hutterites reject living off hire and property and share the fruits of common labour, though Acts distributes by need.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Hutterites hold nonresistance even against attack, and the Diggers acted without violence; Muntzer is the exception.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: believers are a brotherhood of the faithful and Winstanley held equality in creation, not national descent.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Hutterites honour martyrs of the faith but not those who die for a nation, as they refuse force.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Muntzer, Winstanley and the Hutterites all see worldly power as opposed to God's order and set communal life against it.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; these groups have no notion of a national homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Hutterites and Diggers sought renewal through exemplary communities, not by capturing a state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: Hutterite worship and the Diggers' faith use traditional language of God as Father.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: Hutterite scripture reading is within patriarchal roles.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: a brotherhood of believers sharing everything excludes national dominance.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: community of goods is universal, not tied to a people's territory.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions are beside the point in communities that reject hired labour, and the sources are silent.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Winstanley's rejection of rulers and landlords and the commons held by the community itself; the term socialist is anachronistic.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the shared-goods ethic of Acts, in which needs are met from a common stock.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Hutterites' internal votes and Winstanley's rejection of rulers, which favour direct communal decision over layered institutions.

municipal-property.rationale: Goods are held in common by the local community, whether the Jerusalem church, a Hutterite colony or a Digger commune.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Hutterite colonies run themselves and cooperate in a wider church; inferred from that.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from distribution to each as he has need, and the Hutterites' family-centred, patriarchal practice.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Hutterites' traditional outlook and their acceptance of life's limits; not discussed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: money is rejected or held in a common treasury, with no place for private, untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the Hutterites' communal oversight and separation from the world.

person-over-state.rationale: Believers give up private goods for the community, yet reject coercive rulers; the strands do not give one answer.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement is founded on religion, treating common ownership as a commandment of faith.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Unaddressed; these groups reject or withdraw from the state.

gm-crops.rationale: Unaddressed; Hutterites farm with modern methods but sources do not discuss it.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the communal rural farming of the Hutterites and Diggers; not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement's shared-goods ethic is universal among believers and Winstanley held all equal in creation.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the universal framing of faith and equality in Acts and Winstanley; not addressed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Hutterites and Diggers renounce force, and the sources contrast Müntzer's armed variant as exceptional.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the Acts church was a fellowship of believers open to all peoples, and its communities define themselves by faith, not language or nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Hutterites and Diggers withdraw from state politics or address all people in common, and the sources never discuss separate electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: these communities keep apart from national politics and the sources show no belief in foreign plots against a country.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the principle that goods and services are shared by need, though Hutterites run their own schools and the sources do not discuss public colleges.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The sources never address environmental taxation, and communities of goods would split between pricing and communal restraint.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: Winstanley called the earth a common treasury for all, which implies a duty not to ruin it for others.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not address women's distinct values; Hutterites keep distinct gender roles while Diggers and others stress common equality.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Hutterites and Diggers renounce force and bear no arms, so they favour minimal armaments, though Müntzer's wing took up arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The sources do not mention diplomacy, and communities that withdraw from the state take no position on treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: groups that reject buying, selling and money as a betrayal of faith would welcome limits on the flow of capital, but the sources do not address it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Nonresistant groups withdraw from state affairs while Müntzer's movement took up arms; sources do not address who may bear arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Hutterites hold nonresistance and refuse military service, and the Diggers renounced force, though Müntzer's strand fought.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Winstanley rejected hired labour altogether, so bargaining over wages is beside the point; sources are silent.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Topping up wages presumes the wage system that these groups reject as a betrayal of faith; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by these communities; no basis to lean either way.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The groups seek withdrawal into communities of goods, not reform of international economic rules; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Müntzer's strand sought to overthrow rulers, but Hutterites withdraw from the state and the Diggers acted nonviolently; the family is split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The groups hold that believers should share goods in common as a model, not leave economic form open; inferred from Acts and Winstanley.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Winstanley called the earth a common treasury not to be bought and sold, which is at odds with pricing nature as an asset; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Hutterites separate from worldly institutions and Winstanley condemned rulers, so a sacred nation is inferred to be foreign to them.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The tradition condemns usury and lending at interest, so relieving loan debts is inferred to be welcome.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the groups criticise exploitation by the rich generally, not by regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Winstanley grounds equality in all people's common creation by God, and Acts treats believers as sharing one standing before God.

public-service-media.rationale: No view on media; separatist communities like the Hutterites avoid worldly media, others are silent.

missingStatements.text: Believers should live in a community where members hold their goods in common.
missingStatements.rationale: Acts 2:44 and 4:32 describe believers holding all things common, and Hutterites still live this way.

missingStatements.text: No person should work for hire for another or rent land from another.
missingStatements.rationale: Winstanley pledged to work together without giving or taking hire.

missingStatements.text: The Earth belongs to all people in common and should not be bought and sold.
missingStatements.rationale: Winstanley called the earth a common treasury and condemned its sale to a few.

notes: Strands differ on violence (Hutterites and Diggers nonresistant, Müntzer armed) and on gender (Hutterites patriarchal, Taborites and Winstanley egalitarian). Many modern policy answers are inferred from the Hutterites' conservative practice. Sources on Wikipedia, Hutterite and Christian communism pages were read in part only (first 100,000 characters).
